key_insight: High-order surface finite elements paired with stabilized time integrators model conserved phase separation on curved closed surfaces while providing discrete mass and energy guarantees.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports accurate simulation of composition evolution on curved interfaces where geometry, conservation, and numerical stability matter.
method: Mixed hp-surface finite elements with curvilinear high-order geometry.
Stabilized semi-implicit BDF2 and convex-splitting variants using the same factorization.
Discrete analysis of mass conservation, energy balance, and conditional modified-energy decay.
evidence_signal: Manufactured solutions verify second-order time accuracy and expected h/p convergence; torus interface energies and higher-genus unstable-mode counts match reference estimates within 1%, with higher-genus mass conserved to roundoff.
watch_item: The semi-implicit energy guarantees require the stated potential and nonlinear truncation assumptions, and modified-energy monotonicity is conditional.
paper_title: Semi-Implicit and Convex Splitting Schemes for the Surface Cahn--Hilliard Equation on Curved Closed Surfaces
